tools.name: check_dependencies
tools.description: Check a dependency manifest (package.json, requirements.txt, pyproject.toml or Pipfile) for third-party API SDKs that are major versions behind, deprecated or replaced, against the live npm registry and PyPI. Returns each SDK's current spec, latest version, release-notes link and a Versyka migration

tools.name: find_retired_models
tools.description: Scan source and config files for AI model IDs that the vendor (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Mistral, Cohere, xAI, DeepSeek) or hosting platform (Amazon Bedrock, Groq, Fireworks AI, Google Vertex AI) has retired or scheduled for retirement. Exact matches only, including Bedrock, Vertex AI, LiteL

tools.name: lookup_model
tools.description: Is this AI model ID retired or scheduled for retirement? Accepts plain IDs and gateway spellings (e.g. openai/gpt-4-0613, anthropic.claude-3-sonnet-20240229-v1:0, claude-3-opus@20240229). Returns the shutdown date, status, replacement and source, or that no retirement is listed.

tools.name: list_model_retirements
tools.description: The AI model retirement calendar: model IDs with their shutdown dates, replacements and sources, soonest first. Filter by vendor or by how many days ahead to look.

tools.name: get_sdk_versions
tools.description: The latest version of an npm or PyPI package, whether it is deprecated, its release-notes link, the API vendor it belongs to and a Versyka migration guide when one exists.

tools.name: list_migration_guides
tools.description: Versyka's step-by-step SDK migration guides (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, AWS, Stripe, Firebase, Slack, Twilio, Auth0, Pinecone), optionally filtered by package name.

tools.name: get_migration_guide
tools.description: One migration guide as Markdown: what changed, each step with before and after code, how to find every affected call, how to test, and the vendor sources it is based on.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "find_retired_models" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
